revision_note: Re-verified 2026-08-02 against the same defect class as exclusion-depth-fork-001 (a wrong-policy digest pinned without naming its algorithm). No defect found: this KAT already scopes each digest to a named algorithm, and it is the discriminator BETWEEN the two algorithms, so there is no third output to carry. v2 adds the explicit algorithm/theorem mapping per digest, the pipeline statement, and a recorded normalization-fixpoint check.
source: mm-fail-01 discriminator (jcs-s vs jcs-n), CPB-registry vector set v0.1 (reference: draft-mih-sokolov-scitt-payload-binding-00 §3.1); machine-checked in Lean 4 (jcss/Jcss/Removal.lean; every pinned byte string kernel-checked, axiom closure {propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound}, sorry count 0)

pipeline.jcs-n: CANONICAL-DIGEST(jcs-n, P) = lowercase_hex(SHA-256(JCS(normalize(P)))) — absent-field normalization removes object members whose value is null, an empty array, or an empty object.
pipeline.jcs-s: CANONICAL-DIGEST(jcs-s, P) = lowercase_hex(SHA-256(JCS(P))) — no normalization pass; those members are retained.
pipeline.note: This witness carries no exclusion set: it isolates the member-removal pass alone, independently of the exclusion-depth question tested by exclusion-depth-fork-001.

must_fail.diagnosis: member removal performed while claiming jcs-s
must_fail.policy: bottom-up removal of null / empty-array / empty-object members
must_fail.note: This is the CORRECT jcs-n digest for this witness. It is a MUST-FAIL only for an implementation declaring jcs-s; the entry is a mislabelling discriminator, not an implementation bug in jcs-n.

rule: Implementations of jcs-s MUST retain null / empty-array / empty-object object members. A conforming jcs-s implementation canonicalizing the witness MUST produce 335b45b0.... An implementation producing 99e6326a... is running the jcs-n member-removal pass and MUST FAIL this KAT when it declares jcs-s. Both digests are algorithm-scoped: this vector discriminates jcs-s from jcs-n and each side is the correct output of its own algorithm — neither is a pre-normalization intermediate, so unlike exclusion-depth-fork-001 there is no third output to carry.
normalization_interaction_check: Verified 2026-08-02 that jcs-n normalization does not interact with this witness beyond the modelled removal: normalize(W) = {"d":1}, and normalize(normalize(W)) = {"d":1}, i.e. one pass reaches a fixpoint and no cascade removal occurs (no member becomes empty as a consequence of an inner removal). The result equals the Lean model output Jcss.stripNullsEmpty wNull (theorem Jcss.strip_wNull). Cascade behaviour is exercised separately by Jcss.removal_bottom_up, and the array-element exemption by Jcss.removal_keeps_array_elements.
digests_computed_by: Recomputed 2026-08-02 by two independent implementations that agreed on every byte string and every digest: (1) a standard-library-only Python script (hand-written RFC 8785 serializer for this subset + hashlib); (2) the CPB reference implementation cpb.canonicalize (normalize / jcs / canonical_digest) from scitt-payload-binding. Both agree byte-for-byte with the Lean-pinned strings above, and the digests equal the mm-fail-01 registry fields.
